jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**
===================


For generations, California YMCA Youth \& Government has helped young people discover the power of their voice, understand democracy through experience, and see themselves as leaders capable of shaping their communities and their future.


The Executive Director, California YMCA Youth \& Government will provide strategic and executive leadership for one of the nation’s largest civic education and youth leadership programs, serving thousands of middle and high school students across California. Reporting to the Chief Program Officer of the YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles, the Executive Director will lead the next chapter of a statewide movement built on youth leadership, civic engagement, volunteer service, philanthropy, and the collective strength of YMCA associations throughout California.


This is an external\-facing executive role requiring a leader who can build relationships and inspire investment in the mission. The Executive Director will cultivate donors and philanthropic partners, strengthen and develop the Board of Managers, engage and grow a statewide network of volunteers, build relationships with YMCA associations and civic and community leaders, and ensure the continued quality, relevance, reach, and sustainability of California YMCA Youth \& Government.


At the same time, this leader will provide executive oversight for statewide programs including Model Legislature \& Court (MLC), Model United Nations (MUN), national leadership experiences, and major conferences and events serving thousands of young people.


The successful candidate will understand that the strength of Youth \& Government is not built by staff alone. It is built through people: young leaders, committed volunteers, engaged board members, donors, YMCA partners, educators, civic leaders, alumni, and communities united around a belief in the potential of young people.

**The Leadership Mandate**
==========================


The next Executive Director will be charged with sustaining the extraordinary legacy of California YMCA Youth \& Government while building the relationships, resources, leadership infrastructure, and strategy necessary for its future.


Three areas of executive leadership will be especially critical:

**Philanthropy \& Fund Development**
------------------------------------


The Executive Director will serve as a chief fundraiser and relationship builder for California YMCA Youth \& Government, leading a comprehensive development strategy with an annual goal of generating approximately $480,000 in philanthropic support.


This leader must be comfortable moving from strategy to solicitation. They will cultivate and steward individual donors, pursue major gifts, build corporate and foundation relationships, develop sponsorship opportunities, identify new sources of philanthropic revenue, and create meaningful opportunities for supporters to experience the impact of Youth \& Government firsthand.


Just as importantly, the Executive Director will build a culture of philanthropy around the program, partnering with board members, volunteers, alumni, YMCA leaders, and other champions to expand the network of people willing to invest in its future.

**This is not a position that simply supports fundraising. Fund development is a central executive responsibility of the role.**

**Board Development \& Governance**
-----------------------------------


The Executive Director will serve as the primary staff partner to the California YMCA Youth \& Government Board of Managers, developing a highly engaged board that provides meaningful governance, strategic leadership, philanthropy, advocacy, and community influence.


The Executive Director will lead board recruitment, onboarding, engagement, development, and evaluation while partnering closely with board leadership to establish strategic priorities and measure progress. This leader will strengthen committee structures and charts of work, cultivate future board leadership, and ensure board members have meaningful opportunities to contribute their expertise, relationships, resources, and influence to the mission.


The successful candidate will understand the difference between managing a board and developing one. We are seeking an executive who can build a strong partnership with volunteer governance leaders and help strengthen a board that is engaged, accountable, connected, and actively advancing the organization.

**Volunteer Leadership \& Development**
---------------------------------------


Volunteers are fundamental to the identity, culture, reach, and success of California YMCA Youth \& Government.


The Executive Director will lead a statewide volunteer engagement strategy that honors and retains the dedicated volunteers who have built and sustained this program while intentionally recruiting and developing the next generation of volunteer leaders.


This requires more than volunteer coordination. It requires an executive who understands volunteerism at the highest level and knows how to create an environment where people choose to give their time, expertise, relationships, and leadership year after year.


The Executive Director will strengthen the full volunteer experience, including recruitment, engagement, development, communication, recognition, leadership pathways, succession, and retention. This leader must be equally skilled at honoring institutional knowledge and longstanding relationships while welcoming new voices, new perspectives, and new volunteers into the movement.

jobs.description:
**Position:** Deputy Director of Policy and Political Campaigns

**Location:** Los Angeles, CA

**Status:** Exempt, Hybrid

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Compensation:** $90,000 \- $110,000

**Advance Policy. Build Power. Create Lasting Change.**

Black Women for Wellness Action Project (BWWAP) is seeking an experienced, strategic Deputy Director of Policy and Political Campaigns to lead the development and execution of our public policy agenda. This is an opportunity to transform community priorities into policy solutions that advance reproductive justice, environmental justice, birth justice, health equity, civic engagement, and economic justice for Black women, girls, and gender\-expansive people.

If you are passionate about advancing bold policy solutions and partnering with communities to dismantle structural inequities, we invite you to join our leadership team.

**About Us**

Black Women for Wellness Action Project is a 501(c)(4\) social welfare organization dedicated to advancing policies and electing leaders who improve the health, well\-being, and quality of life for Black women, girls, and gender\-expansive people.

Our work moves public policy forward, elects leaders who prioritize Black women's needs, shifts culture through media and storytelling, and empowers community members to engage in the fight for equity and justice. Through organizing, advocacy, coalition building, and civic engagement, we are building political power that creates lasting systems change.

**Position Summary**

As the Deputy Director of Policy and Political Campaigns, you will serve as the organization's lead policy strategist, shaping legislative priorities and developing advocacy initiatives that center the lived experiences of Black women. Working closely with the Executive Director, Communications Team, and community organizers, you will translate community voices into policy solutions while strengthening relationships with lawmakers, coalition partners, researchers, and advocates.

This role sits at the intersection of public policy, research, advocacy, and movement building, ensuring that Black Women for Wellness Action Project remains a trusted voice in shaping policies that improve health and racial equity throughout California.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead the development and implementation of the organization's legislative and public policy agenda.
* Monitor and analyze local, state, and federal legislation to identify opportunities, challenges, and emerging policy issues.
* Develop policy briefs, testimony, reports, fact sheets, and recommendations that support advocacy and legislative priorities.
* Build and maintain relationships with policymakers, government agencies, coalition partners, and community stakeholders to advance shared policy goals.
* Represent the organization at legislative hearings, policy tables, public meetings, and advocacy coalitions.
* Collaborate across organizing, political, communications, and development teams to ensure policy strategies align with organizational campaigns and community priorities.
* Supervise policy staff, consultants, interns, and cross\-functional workgroups while fostering collaboration and professional growth.
* Ensure policy and advocacy activities comply with applicable nonprofit regulations and advance the organization's strategic objectives.

**Who You Are**

You are a collaborative leader who understands that meaningful policy begins with community voice. You are equally comfortable analyzing legislation, facilitating coalition meetings, briefing elected officials, and translating complex policy into clear, actionable recommendations.

**What You’ll Bring**

* Eight to twelve years of experience in public policy, legislative affairs, government relations, advocacy, or nonprofit leadership.
* Demonstrated success developing policy agendas, advancing legislative priorities, and influencing public policy.
* Strong understanding of California's legislative and regulatory processes.
* Experience building diverse coalitions and cultivating partnerships across government, philanthropy, academia, and community organizations.
* Exceptional research, writing, public speaking, and strategic communication skills.
* Experience supervising teams and managing complex policy initiatives.
* A deep commitment to racial justice, reproductive justice, health equity, civic engagement, and Black women's leadership.
* A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required; a Master's in Public Policy (MPP), Public Administration (MPA), Political Science, Law (JD), or a related field is strongly preferred.

**Why Black Women for Wellness Action Project?**

At BWWAP, policy is grounded in community. We believe Black women are experts in their own lived experiences, and we work every day to ensure those experiences shape the laws, systems, and institutions that impact our lives.

As Policy Director, you will help drive transformational change by developing policies that improve health outcomes, expand opportunity, strengthen democracy, and advance justice for Black women and our communities.

If you're ready to help shape the future of California through bold policy leadership, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and help us build healthier communities, stronger policies, and a more just future for Black women and generations to come.

**About:**

The Women’s Prison Association (WPA) was founded in 1845 in New York City by Quaker abolitionist and prison reformer Abigail Hopper Gibbons. Established in response to the overcrowded and inhumane conditions in New York jails, WPA sought to support incarcerated women, who at the time were often considered “unredeemable.” It was the first organization dedicated to the rights and rehabilitation of system\-involved women.

Today, decarceration is our North Star. Based in New York City, WPA strives to make the incarceration of women obsolete. We operate on a gender\-responsive, trauma\-informed model of support that provides the essential services justice\-impacted women need to remain in their communities, heal, and thrive.

WPA is at an exciting and pivotal moment in its evolution. In 2025, WPA adopted a transformative 3\-year strategic plan centered around three impact goals:

* Create a comprehensive, high\-quality service model, prioritizing housing support and essential care for justice\-impacted women.
* Weave an effective, robust community support network so that justice\-impacted women receive the opportunities, services, and gender\-responsive care they need.
* Shift public opinion and justice system practices and policies so that community\-based support, and not incarceration, is the default response to contact with the criminal legal system.

As the organization advances, this role will contribute to WPA's continued growth and stability.

The Impact You Will Own

Lead and optimize a diverse portfolio of services—from 25\+ residential programs to clinical, vocational, day habilitation, educational divisions—ensuring consistency, quality, and full utilization across all lines.
  
* Strategic Execution That Delivers Results


Translate vision into action—driving clear goals, accountability structures, and outcomes across Vice Presidents, Directors, and Principals.

Build and coach high\-performing senior leaders who can scale impact, strengthen culture, and drive accountability across the organization.
  
* Innovation \& Growth


Identify new service opportunities, expand programs, and play a key role in initiatives like Black Water Acres, a first\-of\-its\-kind accessible workforce and community development project.
  
* System Integration


Break down silos and create a coordinated, person\-centered service model that improves outcomes for the people we support.
  
  

Why This Role Is Different
  
Most COO roles maintain. This one builds.

* Partner directly with the CEO and Board to shape long\-term strategy

* Lead in a space where purpose and performance must coexist—and both matter equally

* A strategic operator who turns vision into execution

* Financially fluent, with a deep understanding of budgets, margins, and performance drivers
* Mission\-driven, with a genuine commitment to disability rights, inclusion, and person\-centered care

* Increased program utilization and operational efficiency

**Chief Operating Officer (COO)**


***Lead a Mission. Transform a System. Build What’s Next.***


**Location:** Western New York (Buffalo Region)  

**Compensation:** $160,000 – $180,000 \+ Executive Benefits

  


**This Is Not a Traditional COO Role**



This is an opportunity to **reshape how an entire system of care operates**—not just manage it.



At **The Arc Erie County New York**, we serve individuals with developmental disabilities across residential, clinical, educational, and community\-based programs. Our next Chief Operating Officer will do more than oversee operations—they will **define what operational excellence looks like in a mission\-driven organization for the next decade.**



You will step into a system with strong foundations and be expected to **elevate performance, unify services, and unlock growth opportunities** across a complex, multi\-division organization.



This role is for a leader driven to elevate and leave a lasting impact\- not simply maintain the status quo. It requires a genuine passion for improving the lives of children and adults with developmental disabilities and a deep connection to the mission we serve every day.

Lead and optimize a diverse portfolio of services—from 25\+ residential programs to clinical, vocational, day habilitation, educational divisions—ensuring consistency, quality, and full utilization across all lines.

* **System Integration**  

Break down silos and create a **coordinated, person\-centered service model** that improves outcomes for the people we support.

Most COO roles maintain. ***This one builds.***

* Partner directly with the CEO and Board to shape long\-term strategy
* Influence systems governed by complex regulatory environments (OPWDD, NYSED, Medicaid)
* Lead in a space where **purpose and performance must coexist—and both matter equally**

* Financially fluent, with a deep understanding of **budgets, margins, and performance drivers**

* Increased program utilization and operational efficiency
* Strengthened leadership accountability across all divisions
* Clear, measurable performance standards tied to outcomes
* Enhanced employee engagement and retention strategies
* Identifiable growth opportunities and program expansion pathways

**Description:**  

Mercy Care Atlanta is for a dynamic and transformational executive to serve as its next Chief Operating Officer.
  
  

Position Purpose
  
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior executive responsible for leading and optimizing day\-to\-day operations across multiple clinic sites in Atlanta and Chamblee, GA. Reporting to the Mercy Care Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the COO serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO helping to drive key organizational priorities, enhance operational effectiveness, and ensure alignment with Mercy Care’s mission and strategic direction. The COO also acts as a liaison across executive leadership, coordinates special initiatives of the CEO, and oversees the efficacy of the Office of the CEO.
  
  

**Mercy Care:**  

Mercy Care is a nonprofit community health organization that provides primary care, dental, vision, behavioral health, pediatric and pharmacy services for underserved populations, especially people who are uninsured, underinsured experiencing homelessness or poverty. It is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) and has a 340B Pharmacy.
  
  

Mercy Care supports the comprehensive needs of its patients providing extensive social supports this includes case management, substance abuse counseling, recuperative care individuals being discharged from the hospital, intensive supports for high utilizers of emergency departments of local hospitals. Mercy Care has been serving Atlanta since 1985\.
  
  

**Mercy Care Mission:** Furthering the healing ministry of the Sisters of Mercy, Mercy Care gives tangible expression to Christ’s merciful love by promoting health and health equity and providing compassionate, clinically excellent healthcare in the spirit of loving service to those in need, with special attention to the poor and vulnerable.
  
  

**Mercy Care Vision:** Mercy Care will provide affordable, compassionate and excellent care to its patients, leading to improved health. jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
jobs.description:
The Islamic Association of Raleigh (IAR) is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Chief Executive Officer to oversee, manage, coordinate, and administer all IAR operations in accordance with the organization’s established and approved goals. This pivotal leadership role serves as the primary administrative and operational leader of one of the largest and oldest Islamic centers in the Carolinas, reporting directly to the IAR Chairperson and working closely with the Shura.


If you have a proven track record of nonprofit or organizational leadership, managing diverse teams and committees, and representing an organization externally with confidence and integrity, this is an opportunity to lead the strategic direction and day\-to\-day operations of a thriving, growing community institution. The position is full\-time and in\-person, and the final selection of the successful candidate is subject to approval by the IAR Shura.


### **About the Islamic Association of Raleigh (IAR)**


The Islamic Association of Raleigh (IAR) is an Islamic center serving as a mosque, school, and gathering place for the Muslim community in the Research Triangle region of North Carolina. IAR is the largest mosque in the Carolinas and among the oldest in the area, hosting over three thousand congregants every Friday.


### **Responsibilities**


The Chief Executive Officer shall report to the IAR Chairperson and be responsible to:


* Manage the Administration Team and IAR committees.
* Provide guidance and direction to IAR committees to build capacity, strengthen sustainability and increase program impact to the community.
* Prepare a list of short\-term and long\-term activities of IAR needed for executing successful operations.
* Convey the organization vision to all stakeholders internally and externally including staff, partners, donors, community groups and others whose involvement is needed for success.
* Responsible to put actions towards a strategic plan, monitor progress to measure the outcomes and make recommendations to the IAR leadership on any needed course corrections required for successful implementation.
* Identify the resources needed towards the implementation of the strategic plan and budget accordingly while balancing internal and external stakeholder needs.
* Manage administrative staff and volunteers.
* Provide monthly operational and fiscal reports to the Shura Chairperson and attend the Shura meeting.
* Be the main representative and correspondent for the IAR in external affairs.
* Provide annual update on the progression of Shura approved Strategic Plan and make recommendations to refine and update short\-term and long\-term strategic activities of the IAR.
* Be a liaison between the IAR, other organizations and external media.
* The CEO shall have the power and authority to exercise all the rights, powers and authority on all operation matters and in accordance with IAR Constitution.

### **Required Skills and Qualifications**


* B.S./B.A. in business or related field or M.S./M.B.A.
* At least five years of experience in a leadership or managerial role in private or non\-profit organization
* Knowledge and ability to work with various stakeholders in the Muslim and non\-Muslim community.
* A proven ability to lead and mentor others.
* Solid grounding in general principles of Islam.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work effectively with a wide range of constituencies in a diverse community.
* Excellent English written and verbal communication skills

### **Preferred Skills and Qualifications**


* Previous experience or working knowledge of IAR or other similar sized Islamic institution
* Ability to ensure commitment to and compliance with applicable laws and regulations across the organization
* Experience creating and monitoring $1M\+ budgets

### **Salary \& Benefits**


* Salary and benefits commensurate with qualifications, knowledge and experience. To Apply, please
* send your cover letter and resume by email to Jobs@islam1\.org
* No phone calls please. Only finalists will be contacted.

**Position Summary**



The Fort Wayne Philharmonic seeks a dynamic, results\-driven Vice President of Development to lead its comprehensive fundraising program and contribute to the strategic growth and sustainability of one of Indiana’s premier performing arts organizations. The ideal candidate is a visionary leader and accomplished fundraiser with a passion for the arts and a proven record of cultivating transformational relationships with individuals, corporations, and community leaders.

  



Reporting to the President \& CEO and serving as a key member of the Philharmonic’s senior leadership team, the Vice President of Development will lead a department responsible for annual giving, major gifts, capital and endowment campaigns, corporate sponsorship, foundation relations, planned giving, and donor stewardship. The Vice President will inspire and manage a talented team of development professionals and play an integral role in realizing the Philharmonic’s ambitious artistic, educational, and community goals.

  


**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**


*Strategic Fundraising \& Campaign Leadership*


* Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy including capital campaigns, annual fund, major gifts, planned giving, corporate sponsorships, and special events.
* Lead the strategy and operations for multi\-year capital campaigns aligned with the Philharmonic’s historic downtown facility and institutional growth.
* Design fundraising timelines, goals, performance metrics, and reporting tools to evaluate progress and inform future planning.
* Identify, cultivate, and solicit new prospects using donor research, prospect screening, board referrals, and audience engagement data.


*Donor Engagement and Relationship Management*

  

* Create and lead a year\-round calendar of cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship events and activities (visits, calls, letters, and presentations) that deepen donor involvement
* Ensure all donor engagement is meaningful, personalized, and reflects the Philharmonic’s artistic mission and community impact.
* Develop tailored solicitation strategies based on a donor’s experience with the Philharmonic and their giving capacity.
* Oversee strategies to move annual donors, subscribers, and attendees into major gift portfolios.


*Board \& Staff Management*

  

* Educate and engage the Board of Directors, executive leadership, and staff in development strategy and activity, empowering them as ambassadors and fundraisers.
* Report regularly on development progress and goals to internal stakeholders and the Board.


*Collaborative Leadership \& Management*

  

* Manage a high\-performing Development team through thoughtful goal\-setting, coaching, performance evaluation, and mentorship.
* Oversee donor database (CRM) strategy and execution in collaboration with the Director of Consumer Engagement to ensure accurate records, segmentation, and analytics.
* Partner with Marketing and Sales teams to co\-create and promote fundraising events and campaigns that drive both visibility and support.
* Represent the Philharmonic at performances, civic events, donor functions, and community activities to build relationships and represent the organization.


*Additional Details*


* Create and deliver compelling in\-person presentations to high\-level audiences in support of Philharmonic projects and priorities.
* Stay informed on national trends in philanthropy, arts fundraising, and donor engagement.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the CEO to advance the Philharmonic’s mission and values.

  


**Requirements**


* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or CFRE preferred.
* Minimum 7\+ years of progressive fundraising leadership experience, ideally in the performing arts or nonprofit sector.
* Demonstrated success in major gifts, corporate sponsorship, capital campaigns, and special events.
* Proven ability to manage and inspire teams and lead through change.
* Strong interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills.
* High emotional intelligence and a collaborative spirit.
* Experience with CRM systems (e.g., Tessitura, Raiser’s Edge) and proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
* Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends at concerts and events.
* Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel as needed within the region

  


**Organization Description**  

Now in its 83rd season, the Fort Wayne Philharmonic is one of the most exciting performing arts organizations in Indiana. The Philharmonic’s mission is to inspire and foster a lifelong love of classical music through performance and education. Led by Music Director Andrew Constantine, the Philharmonic performances reach more than 200,000 people every season at the majestic Embassy Theatre, the Auer Concert Hall, and at various venues throughout the community, including schools, nursing homes, community centers, and churches.

  



The Fort Wayne Philharmonic is truly an orchestra of the future, with bold plans to reach deeply into the fabric of the community with exciting, entertaining and meaningful offerings. The Philharmonic reaches more than 39,000 young people and families through its extensive education and community engagement programs, including Ensembles in the Schools, Young People’s Concerts, and Club Orchestra \- a novel El Sistema modeled collaborative program with 3 Fort Wayne Community Schools \- inspiring and motivating young citizens of the future. Regional touring, donor cultivation, and board activities round out a busy performance schedule for the orchestra.

The Director of Communications reports to the Executive Director of MURR and also has reporting responsibilities to the Senior Director of Marketing and Communications.  

The Director of Communications is a member of the MURR leadership team and will collaborate with MURR and NextGen MURR senior management, researchers, university communicators, government relations and industry partners to provide a multi\-channel communications strategy that effectively raises awareness of MURR and NextGen MURR among target audiences.
